subject: Evaluation alignment — performance benchmarks & close timeline
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, May 01, 2026 at 09:12 AM PDT
Subject: Initial MAP deliverable — baseline benchmarks + proposed close timeline

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Attached are the baseline benchmark artifacts we ran as part of the MAP: redwood-bench-results-20260501.csv and the MAP_v3-FinTechCo.pdf which includes the evaluation plan and proposed close timeline. High-level summary:

- Model variant: open-xlarge-v2 (fp16, 16-bit kernels)
- Test hardware: 2x A100-80GB (no MIG), single-GPU runs for p95 profiling, multi-GPU for throughput scaling
- Workload: FinTechCo prompt set (50k tokens aggregate), average prompt length 78 tokens
- Batching: continuous batching enabled, dynamic batch size 1-16
- Caching: prefix KV cache enabled for repeated session prefixes

Results (representative):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): median 18ms, p95 42ms
- Latency (per-token p50/p95): 12ms / 38ms
- Throughput: sustained 68k tokens/min per GPU at concurrency 12
- Concurrency sweep: stable up to 16 concurrent user sessions before p95 degradation >20%

Notes / known differences in our runs: we ran with continuous batching and prefix caching turned on (this improves unit cost but can lower TTFT under some arrival patterns). We used our internal load generator (loadgen v4) with request arrival modeled as Poisson; we used your shared prompt set but normalized tokenization with our tokenizer (we included the tokenize mapping in repro-instructions.txt).

Ask / proposed next steps (MAP milestones):
1) You confirm whether FinTechCo will supply a trimmed prompt set (we can run the full set if preferred) or if you want us to use the CSV provided. (by EOD May 2)
2) We run an alignment reproduction with the exact prompts and arrival pattern you want (2 business days).
3) Deliver a reconciled benchmark report +/- config diffs and a recommended production profile (EOD May 5).
4) Canary plan + SLA T&Cs drafted for signature (target close: May 7).

If we can't reproduce your numbers we will triage: (a) customer repro (we run with exact prompts/harness), (b) tooling differences (loadgen vs JMeter/wrk), (c) model variant / quantization mismatch, (d) infra differences (MIG, NIC tuning).

I've cc'd Marissa and Rishi to help with repro and competitive checks. Let us know which arrival pattern you want us to use for the reproduction run.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0139

Attachments: redwood-bench-results-20260501.csv; MAP_v3-FinTechCo.pdf; repro-instructions.txt
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@fintechco.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Ramesh <priya.r@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, May 01, 2026 at 11:04 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Initial MAP deliverable — baseline benchmarks + proposed close timeline

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick turn. A couple of things stood out when my infra team ran a dry pass with our harness:

- Our p95 numbers are ~1.6x higher than yours at concurrency 8 (we see p95 ~62ms).
- We ran on 1x A100-80GB but with NVLINK aggregated across a small cluster (our prod-like setup is 1 GPU per pod with autoscaling).
- Important: our latency distribution has a long tail when short prompts (<=32 tokens) are interleaved with long prompts (>=200 tokens).

Can you reproduce with: (1) our exact prompt csv (we'll upload a trimmed 5k sample), (2) arrival model = bursty with microbursts (not Poisson), (3) single-GPU pod topology (i.e., no multi-GPU aggregation)?

Also, we run wrk-based harness instrumented with OpenTelemetry; curious if your loadgen timestamps align to our tracing. If you can reproduce and reconcile tooling differences by Monday morning we can keep the May 7 close target. Otherwise we may need an extra week for SOC review sign-off.

Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of ML Engineering, FinTechCo
samir.gupta@fintechco.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, May 03, 2026 at 08:22 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Initial MAP deliverable — baseline benchmarks + proposed close timeline

Samir —

Appreciate the detail — we can definitely run the reproduction per your exact constraints. Action plan below (will update MAP_v3 after we agree):

Reproduction plan (2 business days):
- Ingest FinTechCo 5k prompt sample (exact tokens) — you said you'll upload to the Drive link, will confirm when present.
- Topology: single-GPU pod runs (A100-80GB), no NVLINK aggregation; replicate your autoscaling disabled for the run.
- Arrival pattern: bursty microbursts (we'll use a tuned wrk profile to match your OpenTelemetry-ready harness so timestamps are comparable).
- Tooling: we will run both wrk and our loadgen to instrument differences; all runs will emit OpenTelemetry spans to the same collector so you can compare traces.
- Config toggles: runs with prefix KV cache ON/OFF, batching continuous ON/OFF, quantization fp16 vs int8-quant.

Deliverables and updated MAP milestones:
- Monday EOD (May 3): confirm prompt upload + repro schedule
- Wed AM (May 5): reproduction runs complete + raw artifacts uploaded
- Wed EOD (May 5): reconciled report with delta analysis + recommended production profile
- Thu (May 6): short sync to review canary plan and final SLA language
- Target contract close: Fri (May 7) if reconciled report aligns with your acceptance criteria

If reproduction shows our previous config (continuous batching + caching) is the root cause, we will provide a config recipe to meet your p95 objective (may trade unit cost vs lower TTFT). If the difference is tooling/timestamping, we'll provide an aligned trace-based comparison and a small change-set you can apply to your harness to match our measurement methodology.

I'll start the runs as soon as the sample is uploaded. Marissa / Rishi / Monica — please take ownership of the run matrix and put the initial artifacts in the Drive folder.

Thanks,
Jonas
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, May 03, 2026 at 09:05 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Reproduction plan + triage notes (internal)

Internal quick note:

- Competitor checks: we saw competitor-Alpha's public bench that matches FinTechCo's numbers but they ran int8-quantized on a custom kernel optimized for short-token tails — call that out in delta.
- Tokenizer mismatch: ensure we apply the same normalization (we saw a 4% token count difference due to URL handling).
- Tracing: agree to emit OTEL spans from both harnesses; prepare a simple script to align span timestamps and compute p95 using the same boundary conditions.
- Suggested matrix: wrk vs loadgen, cache on/off, batching on/off, fp16 vs int8, prompt-length buckets (<=32, 33-199, >=200).

I'll prep the comparison table and sample scripts (putting everything into the Drive folder). Marissa — can you run the wrk profile first thing and upload raw traces? Monica — please draft the canary playbook for Thu.

Rishi
Head of Applied ML
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@fintechco.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Ramesh <priya.r@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, May 03, 2026 at 04:22 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Initial MAP deliverable — baseline benchmarks + proposed close timeline

Jonas / team —

Thank you. We've uploaded the 5k sample to the Drive link and set the arrival pattern profile (burst-4 microbursts per second, 120 reqs/s peak). We'll review the OTEL spans as they come in.

Two quick asks before your Wed report:
1) Can you include a short section on how autoscaling would behave in production vs single-GPU pod (we care about warmup effects and cold starts)?
2) For the canary plan, include rollback criteria tied to p95 > 1.4x baseline or error rate > 0.5%.

If the Wed reconciled report confirms we can meet the p95 objective with the config recipe, we are ok to target May 7 close and start the SOC review.

Samir
